title: m7_raw.py has uncommented !pip shell-magic lines - it is not valid Python (SyntaxError)
description: Lines 2-4 and 17-23 are raw IPython/Jupyter shell-magic ('!pip install ...') left uncommented. As a .py module this is a SyntaxError: CPython cannot parse, import, or run the file at all. Confirms it is an unconverted notebook cell dump. This is unique among the dead group - the machine-converted sibling m7_mps.py has these exact lines commented out ('# !pip ...' at its L2-4/L17-23).
evidence: L2 '!pip install --upgrade jinja2 -q', L3-4, L17-19, L22-23 all begin with '!'; contrast m7_mps.py L2-4/L17-23 which are commented.
fix: None if the file is deleted (recommended, see DEAD-001). If retained, every '!' line must be commented. Never try to import it to 'check' it.

title: m7_mps.py is a dead machine-generated MPS clone that runs a training smoke-test on import
description: MPS port of m7_raw.py produced by convert_mps.py; re-defines the same 7 core classes plus legacy zoo and ablations (class defs L633-2944), superseded by code/m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py (which already auto-selects MPS). No __main__ guard: at module scope (L560-576) it seeds, builds M7_ContinualAdaptiveModel and ContinualLearner, and calls trainer.train_task(...), preceded by tonic dataset loading - so 'import m7_mps' downloads datasets and starts training (the same import-time hazard as the live m7_trimodal_run.py trap).
evidence: module-scope execution L560-576: torch.manual_seed L560-561, model_smoke=M7_ContinualAdaptiveModel(...) L569, trainer=ContinualLearner(...) L572, result_smoke=trainer.train_task(...) L576; grep '__main__' returns 0.

title: m7_mps.py has drifted from its generator m7_raw.py and is no longer reproducible by convert_mps.py
description: m7_mps.py is meant to be a pure machine translation of m7_raw.py via convert_mps.py, but the two have diverged: the !pip lines are COMMENTED in m7_mps.py (L2-4/L17-23) yet UNCOMMENTED in m7_raw.py, and convert_mps.py never edits pip lines - so the current m7_mps.py cannot have been produced by running convert_mps.py on the current m7_raw.py. Regenerating is also unsafe because convert_mps.py's exact-string targets are themselves stale (see DEAD-011). Treat m7_mps.py as an orphaned snapshot, not a derived file that can be rebuilt.
evidence: m7_raw.py L2 '!pip...' vs m7_mps.py L2 '# !pip...'; convert_mps.py performs no pip edits (only device/seed/cache/print blocks, L14-167).
fix: Delete m7_raw.py and m7_mps.py together; do not attempt to reconcile or regenerate. Maintained source is m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py.

title: m7_trimodal_cl.py manufactures paper_tables.tex and 'N x more efficient' energy figures from an analytical estimate
description: On import it computes an analytical SynOps energy estimate, renders it as per-inference pJ and a figure titled '... x more efficient' (fig_energy.pdf, last ~25 lines), and writes LaTeX paper_tables.tex (L3465-3577). These are analytical/simulator numbers, not measured hardware energy (contested-facts item 6: a simulator cannot produce energy figures; RULE 1: no number without a CSV). If this dead script is re-run and its output lifted into the paper, it injects unsourced energy/efficiency claims. Retirement should remove this number-manufacturing path, not just the clutter.

fix: Delete the file; never reuse its energy/table output. Any energy number must originate from a CSV per RULE 1.

title: convert_mps.py is a dead one-off codegen whose only output (m7_mps.py) is also dead
description: One-off script that string-transforms m7_raw.py into m7_mps.py. Both its input (m7_raw.py) and output (m7_mps.py) are retired notebook monoliths superseded by code/m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py, which already auto-selects MPS then CUDA then CPU. The tool has no remaining purpose.
evidence: reads m7_raw.py L7-8; writes m7_mps.py L173-174.

title: convert_mps.py overwrites code/m7_mps.py on import (no __main__ guard)
description: All work runs at module scope: it reads m7_raw.py (L7-8) and unconditionally writes/overwrites code/m7_mps.py (L173-174) with no guard, no backup, and no confirmation. Any 'import convert_mps' (for example a tool statically importing code/ modules) silently regenerates m7_mps.py - and because the current m7_raw.py has uncommented !pip lines, the regenerated file would differ from the current one, worsening the drift in DEAD-004. Violates the repo rule against overwriting a file without showing a diff.
evidence: no __main__ (grep returns 0); read at L7-8; open('m7_mps.py','w') + f.write(code) at L173-174, all at column 0.
fix: If retained, wrap the body in if __name__=='__main__': and write to a temp path / print a diff first. Preferred: delete the file.

title: convert_mps.py's exact-string .replace() transforms silently no-op when m7_raw.py drifts
description: The port relies on brittle literal .replace()/regex edits with no verification that any substitution matched. Two are already stale versus current m7_raw.py: (a) the EmbeddingReplayBuffer target expects a 'device=None' third line (convert_mps L91-93) but m7_raw L1774-1776 has 'device: str = 'cuda'', and the regex at L70-84 only matches bare device='cuda' (not the annotated form), so neither the regex nor the exact block fires and auto-detect is never inserted; (b) the ContinualLearner target expects '... device=None, lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4, gradient_clip=1.0' (L102-103) but m7_raw L1883-1884 is '... device='cuda', replay_batch=32, replay_weight=0.3'. A regenerated m7_mps.py would silently keep a CUDA default and break on MPS/CPU, with no error raised. This is why regeneration is unsafe (DEAD-004).
evidence: convert_mps L70-84 regex; L91-99 old_er_init; L102-108 old_cl_init; vs m7_raw L1774-1776 (device: str = 'cuda') and L1883-1884 (device='cuda', replay_batch=32, replay_weight=0.3).
fix: Delete. If a similar tool is ever needed, assert each replacement changed the text (count matches) and fail loudly on zero matches; never patch a moving source with literal strings.

title: modify_notebook.py reads and overwrites a notebook in place on import, with no backup
description: No __main__ guard: at module scope it reads the notebook (L8-9) and at the end writes json.dump back to the SAME path (L563-564) with no backup copy. Were the target present, 'import modify_notebook' would destructively rewrite it. Today it crashes first (DEAD-012), but the destructive read-then-overwrite-in-place pattern is the hazard to retire. Violates the repo rule against overwriting a file without showing a diff.
evidence: read open('r') L8; write open('w') + json.dump(nb, f) L563-564, same filename; grep '__main__' returns 0.
fix: Delete/archive. If ever adapted, write to a NEW path and never overwrite the source in place.

title: modify_notebook.py sets a cell's source to a list of single characters (list(str))
description: src_text is a STRING (built at L207 as ''.join(src) and mutated via .replace()). At L558 the modified source is stored as cells[cl_cell_idx]['source'] = list(src_text), which splits the string into a list of individual CHARACTERS, not lines. The resulting notebook cell 'source' would be thousands of one-character strings - malformed for nbformat and unusable. Unreachable today because L9 crashes first (DEAD-012), but a genuine logic defect unique to this file.
fix: Use src_text.splitlines(keepends=True) (or store the string directly) instead of list(...). Moot if the file is deleted.

title: monitor_and_stop.py is a dead one-off log-watcher tied to a machine that no longer exists
description: A throwaway watcher that tailed one training log and killed one PID during an Era-1 run. It references a foreign absolute log path (/Users/agent1/...) and a fixed PID that have no meaning in this repo, and there is no train.log here. No reusable value.
evidence: LOG_FILE=/Users/agent1/.../train.log L9; PID=16672 L12; regex parses 'Val: NN.N%' L25.

title: monitor_and_stop.py can send kill -15/-9 to an unrelated process (hardcoded PID 16672)
description: PID is hardcoded to 16672 (L12). Inside an infinite 'while True' loop (L33) it watches a foreign log (L9, which never exists here, so get_latest_val_accuracies returns [] and the process loops forever). If the plateau condition were ever met it runs 'kill -15 16672' (L44) then 'kill -9 16672' (L48). On any machine PID 16672 is whatever process currently holds that id - potentially an unrelated user process - so running this can terminate the wrong process. PIDs are not stable identifiers.
evidence: PID=16672 L12; subprocess.run(['kill','-15',str(PID)]) L44; subprocess.run(['kill','-9',str(PID)]) L48; while True L33; foreign LOG_FILE L9.
fix: Delete. Never signal a process by a hardcoded literal PID.

title: benchmark_mps_real.py hardcodes another user's machine path and an MPS-only device
description: L6 does sys.path.insert(0, /Users/agent1/Documents/neuromorphic/m7-trimodal-cl) - a foreign absolute path from a different developer's machine that does not exist here; the subsequent legacy imports (L9-11) depend on it and will ModuleNotFoundError on this repo. L15 hardcodes DEVICE=torch.device('mps') with no CUDA/CPU fallback, so it also crashes on any non-Apple-Silicon host. The file cannot run anywhere as written.
fix: Delete. If ever revived, derive paths relative to the repo and auto-select the device MPS then CUDA then CPU.
